entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Máng of Xia was the ninth king of the semi-legendary Xia dynasty, ruling for approximately 18 years. He was also known as Huang (荒). Máng's reign is marked by a series of significant events, including the construction of the Great Wall of China's earliest version and the establishment of a standardized system of weights and measures.

As king, Máng oversaw the development of agriculture in northern China, introducing new crops and irrigation techniques that increased food production. His military campaigns expanded Xia's borders, but ultimately led to his downfall when he was defeated by the neighboring kingdom of Shang.

Máng's legacy can be seen in the continued use of the standardized system of weights and measures he established, as well as the influence of his agricultural innovations on subsequent Chinese dynasties. Despite his significant impact, Máng's reign remains shrouded in myth and legend, with many details lost to history.

Máng's story serves as a testament to the enduring power of human ingenuity and perseverance, even in the face of adversity.
